sponsors.name: Durtpoo
sponsors.description: Flannel-fresh deep clean in a sixteen-ounce bottle nobody asked for. Notes of aged whiskey, iron, and campfire, which is a polite way of saying it smells like the shed. Lathers generously, regardless of whether there is anything present to lather.
sponsors.testimonial: I have used Durtpoo every morning for a month and my head has never been cleaner. My head has also never had hair. I am not saying these facts are related. I am saying they are both true.
sponsors.imageAlt: Vintage-style advertisement: SnowMan stands in a shower wearing sunglasses and a crown of lather on his bald head, holding a bottle of Durtpoo flannel-fresh deep clean
sponsors.fineprint: Durtpoo is not a real product. SnowMan is a real bald man. No money changed hands in either direction.

sponsors.name: DeadBeat's Detector
sponsors.tagline: Forty years of searching. One class ring. Not mine.
sponsors.description: A beach-grade detector sold with headphones, a sand scoop, and no realistic expectation. Sweeps to a depth of ten inches, which is roughly nine inches deeper than anything of value has ever been found. Discriminates between iron, foil, and disappointment, though in practice it reports all three as the same beep. Batteries not included. Hope not included.
sponsors.testimonial: Every beep is a possibility. Statistically, every beep is a bottle cap. But statistically the sun is going to explode and I still go outside.
sponsors.imageAlt: Vintage-style advertisement: DeadBeat leaps into the air on a beach at sunrise wearing a fur trapper hat with the ear flaps flying, oversized headphones, cargo shorts, tube socks and sandals, grinning with delight as he holds a single tiny rusted bottle cap aloft in one hand and a metal detector in the other, beside a bucket brimming with bottle caps and a horseshoe
sponsors.fineprint: DeadBeat's Detector is not a real product. The class ring was real and we gave it back. The bucket of bottle caps is still on a shelf in the garage.
